claim: Designer nucleases have rapidly expanded the way researchers can utilize endogenous DNA repair mechanisms for creating gene knock-outs, reporter gene knock-ins, gene deletions, single nucleotide polymorphisms, and epitope tagged alleles in diverse species.
source: Designer nucleases have rapidly expanded the way in which researchers can utilize endogenous DNA repair mechanisms for creating gene knock-outs, reporter gene knock-ins, gene deletions, single nucleotide polymorphisms, and epitope tagged alleles in diverse species (Bedell et al., 2012; Beumer et al., 2008; Carlson et al., 2012; Geurts et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work demonstrating these applications.

claim: A single dsDNA break in the genome results in increased frequencies of recombination and promotes integration of homologous recombination (HR)-based vectors.
source: A single dsDNA break in the genome results in increased frequencies of recombination and promotes integration of homologous recombination (HR)-based vectors (Hasty et al., 1991; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Orr-Weaver et al., 1981; Rong and Golic, 2000; Shin et al., 2014; Zu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies demonstrating this phenomenon.

claim: In vitro or in vivo linearization of targeting vectors stimulates homology-directed repair (HDR).
source: Additionally, in vitro or in vivo linearization of targeting vectors stimulates homology-directed repair (HDR) (Hasty et al., 1991; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Orr-Weaver et al., 1981; Rong and Golic, 2000; Shin et al., 2014; Zu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies showing this effect.

claim: Xenopus oocytes have the ability to join or recombine linear DNA molecules that contain short regions of homology at their ends.
source: Previous work has shown Xenopus oocytes have the ability to join or recombine linear DNA molecules that contain short regions of homology at their ends, and this activity is likely mediated by exonuclease activity allowing base pairing of the resected homology (Grzesiuk and Carroll, 1987).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work in Xenopus oocytes.

claim: A plasmid donor containing short (≤40 bp) regions of homology to a genomic target site can promote precise integration at the genomic cut site when the donor plasmid is cut adjacent to the homology in Xenopus, silkworm, zebrafish, and mouse cells.
source: More recently, it was shown in Xenopus, silkworm, zebrafish, and mouse cells that a plasmid donor containing short (≤40 bp) regions of homology to a genomic target site can promote precise integration at the genomic cut site when the donor plasmid is cut adjacent to the homology (Aida et al., 2016; Hisano et al., 2015; Nakade et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies in multiple species.

claim: Gene targeting using short homology is likely mediated by the alternative-end joining/microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) pathway or by a single strand annealing (SSA) mechanism.
source: Gene targeting in these studies is likely mediated by the alternative-end joining/microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) pathway or by a single strand annealing (SSA) mechanism (Ceccaldi et al., 2016), collectively referred to as a homology mediated end joining (HMEJ).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to work on DNA repair pathways.

claim: In human cell culture, linear donors using short homology show inefficient integration until homology domains reach ~600 bp.
source: In contrast, in human cell culture, linear donors using a similar strategy with homologous ends have been reported to show inefficient integration until homology domains reach ~600 bp (Zhang et al., 2017), suggesting different repair pathways may predominate depending on cell type.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study in human cells.

claim: In initial reports using short regions of homology for in vivo gene targeting in zebrafish, the level of mosaicism in F0 injected animals was high, resulting in inefficient recovery of targeted alleles through the germline.
source: In the initial reports using short regions of homology for in vivo gene targeting in zebrafish, the level of mosaicism in F0 injected animals was high, resulting in inefficient recovery of targeted alleles through the germline (Aida et al., 2016; Hisano et al., 2015; Luo et al., 2018; Nakade et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple zebrafish studies.

claim: Studies in Drosophila show efficient integration of exogenous DNA in flies and S2 cells using 100 bp homology arms flanked by a CRISPR target site for in vivo homology liberation.
source: Most recently, studies in Drosophila show efficient integration of exogenous DNA in flies and S2 cells using 100 bp homology arms flanked by a CRISPR target site for in vivo homology liberation (Kanca et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a Drosophila study.

claim: The noto exon 1 sgRNA targeting efficiency was 95% as measured by indel formation at 3 dpf.
source: At 3 dpf, 5 larvae were pooled for genomic DNA extraction and PCR to generate a noto exon 1 amplicon. MiSeq analysis showed 95% of the amplified alleles contained indels at the noto sgRNA genomic target site (Supplementary file 1 Table S1-S2).
evidence: The claim is supported by MiSeq sequencing data showing indel frequency.

claim: Injection of the donor cargo DNA together with noto exon 1 sgRNA and Cas9 mRNA resulted in efficient targeted integration, as observed by notochord-specific RFP expression and PCR amplification of junction fragments.
source: Injection into the cytoplasm of the 1 cell stage embryo of the donor cargo DNA together with noto exon 1 sgRNA and Cas9 mRNA resulted in efficient targeted integration, as observed by notochord-specific RFP expression and PCR amplification of junction fragments between the noto gene and the targeting donor (Figure 1a-c; Supplementary file 1 Table S2-S3).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence imaging and PCR data.

claim: The frequency of embryos with notochord-specific RFP expression increased with the length of the homology arm up to 48 bp.
source: The frequency of embryos with notochord-specific RFP expression increased with the length of the homology arm up to 48 bp (Figure 1b), suggesting that longer homology arms promote increased precise integration of the targeting construct.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1b comparing different homology arm lengths.

claim: Junction fragment analysis in RFP expressing embryos injected with the 12 bp homology arm construct revealed precise integration at the 5' end in 56% of the sequenced alleles (5/9 junctions).
source: Junction fragment analysis in the RFP expressing embryos injected with the 12 bp homology arm construct revealed precise integration at the 5' end in 56% of the sequenced alleles (5/9 junctions) (Figure 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: 95% of the recovered alleles following injection with the 24 bp homology arm construct were precise (19/20 junctions).
source: 95% of the recovered alleles following injection with the 24 bp homology arm construct (19/20 junctions) were precise, with the one imprecise allele containing a duplication of the homology domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: 79% of the recovered alleles from embryos injected with 48 bp homology arm construct were precise (15/19 junctions).
source: 79% of the recovered alleles from embryos injected with 48 bp homology arm construct (15/19 junctions) were also precise (Figure 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: The UgRNA does not have predicted targets in the zebrafish, pig, or human genomes.
source: The UgRNA does not have predicted targets in the zebrafish, pig, or human genomes, and in vivo use shows efficient double strand break induction and homology mediated repair at a target site in a fluorescent reporter integrated into the zebrafish noto gene (Wierson et al., 2019a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work and computational prediction.

claim: 21% of injected embryos showed notochord-specific RFP expression when using the UgRNA guide to direct Cas9 double strand break to the vector in vivo.
source: 21% of injected embryos showed notochord-specific RFP expression, suggesting that Cas9 cutting at the vector UgRNA site efficiently exposes the donor vector 5' homology arm and drives precise targeted integration (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c, Supplementary file 1 Tables S2-S3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data.

claim: Injection of 24 or 48 bp homology arm noto 2A-eGFP-SV40 donors resulted in 24% of zebrafish embryos showing extensive reporter expression in the notochord.
source: Injection of 24 or 48 bp homology arm noto 2A-eGFP-SV40 donors resulted in 24% of zebrafish embryos showing extensive reporter expression in the notochord (Figure 3a,e), indicating a similar in frame and precise integration efficiency compared to targeting with the single 5' homology arm 2A-TagRFP-CAAX-SV40 vector (Supplementary file 1 Tables S2-S3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data shown in Figure 3.

claim: When using the UgRNA to liberate the cargo, 24 bp of homology directs targeted integration as efficiently as 48 bp.
source: The results also suggest that when using the UgRNA to liberate the cargo, 24 bp of homology directs targeted integration as efficiently as 48 bp, further reducing the cost of homology arms for construction of targeting vectors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of targeting efficiencies with different homology arm lengths.

claim: Targeting exon 4 of tyr with a 24 bp homology arm 2A-Gal4/VP16-β-actin3'UTR donor in Tg(UAS:mRFP)tpl2 transgenic zebrafish resulted in strong RFP signal in 64% of injected animals.
source: This resulted in strong RFP signal in 64% of tyr injected animals (Figure 3b,e), however, the embryos were highly mosaic, with only 9% of embryos displaying extensive RFP expression throughout most of the pigmented cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data.

claim: Targeting esama exon 2 with 2A-Gal4/VP16 in the Tg(UAS:mRFP)tpl2 transgenic background resulted in 21% of embryos displaying extensive RFP expression specifically in the vasculature.
source: Targeting esama exon 2 with 2A-Gal4/VP16 in the Tg(UAS:mRFP)tpl2 transgenic background resulted in 21% of embryos displaying extensive RFP expression specifically in the vasculature where esama is expressed (Figure 3c,e).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data and imaging.

claim: Targeted integration of a 2A-TagRFP-CAAX-SV40 cassette into exon 2 of cx43.4 with 24 and 48 bp homology arms resulted in 38–56% and 29–47% of injected embryos showing broad RFP expression throughout the nervous system and vasculature.
source: Targeted integration of a 2A-TagRFP-CAAX-SV40 cassette into exon 2 of cx43.4 with 24 and 48 bp homology arms resulted in 38–56% and 29–47% of injected embryos showing broad RFP expression throughout the nervous system and vasculature (Figure 3d,f).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data.

claim: Increasing the length of the 5' and 3' homology arms to 1 kb did not significantly change the frequency of RFP expression compared to 24 bp (p=0.1693) or 48 bp (p=0.6520) at the cx43.4 locus.
source: Increasing the length of the 5' and 3' homology arms to 1 kb did not significantly change the frequency of RFP expression compared to 24 bp (p=0.1693) or 48 bp (p=0.6520) (Figure 3f), with 26–47% of injected embryos showing the expected neuronal and vascular RFP expression pattern (Supplementary file 1 Table S2-S3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis.

claim: Injection without the UgRNA leaves the 1 kb homology circular donor intact and reduced targeting to 0–3% at the cx43.4 locus.
source: Injection without the UgRNA leaves the 1 kb homology circular donor intact, and reduced targeting to 0–3% (Figure 3f Circular HR 1 kb; p=0.0067; Supplementary file 1 Table S2-S3), as expected given the low frequency of homologous recombination in zebrafish embryos.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis.

claim: The frequency of RFP expressing embryos after injection of the linear 1 kb homology arm template was significantly reduced to approximately 5% at the cx43.4 locus.
source: The frequency of RFP expressing embryos after injection of the linear 1 kb homology arm template was significantly reduced to approximately 5% (Figure 3f Linear HR 1 kb; p=0.0111; Supplementary file 1 Table S2-S3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis.

claim: Long homology arms do not enhance the frequency of integration at the genomic target site, compared with short 24 or 48 bp homology arms, when using the UgRNA to target double strand breaks and liberate the donor homology arms in vivo.
source: Together, these results suggest long homology arms do not enhance the frequency of integration at the genomic target site, compared with short 24 or 48 bp homology arms, when using the UgRNA to target double strand breaks and liberate the donor homology arms in vivo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of targeting efficiencies with different homology arm lengths.

claim: Increasing the esama homology arms from 24 bp to 1 kb dramatically increased the percentage of RFP positive embryos from 20–23% to 82–94% (p=0.0001).
source: Increasing the homology arms from 24 bp to 1 kb dramatically increased the percentage of RFP positive embryos, from 20–23% to 82–94% (p=0.0001 Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1 Table S3).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis.

claim: The majority of RFP expression with 1 kb homology arms at esama was not vascular specific, suggesting off-target integration of the Gal4/VP16 cassette.
source: However, the majority of RFP was not vascular specific, suggesting off-target integration of the Gal4/VP16 cassette.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of non-specific RFP expression patterns.

claim: Three out of five (60%) adults from the noto injected embryos that had shown widespread notochord RFP expression transmitted a noto-2A-TagRFP-CAAX tagged allele through the germline.
source: Three out of five (60%) adults from the noto injected embryos that had shown widespread notochord RFP expression transmitted a noto-2A-TagRFP-CAAX tagged allele through the germline (Figure 4, Table 1, Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by germline transmission data.

claim: At the tyr locus, three out of eight (37.5%) embryos raised to adulthood transmitted germline tagged alleles.
source: At the tyr locus, although RFP expression in tyr-2A-Gal4/VP16 injected Tg(UAS:mRFP)tpl2 embryos was highly mosaic, three out of eight (37.5%) embryos raised to adulthood transmitted germline tagged alleles (Figure 4, Table 1, Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by germline transmission data.

claim: For esama, 12/18 (66.7%) adults that displayed widespread vasculature RFP expression as embryos transmitted esama-2A-Gal4/VP16 alleles to their F1 progeny.
source: For esama, 12/18 (66.7%) adults that displayed widespread vasculature RFP expression as embryos transmitted esama-2A-Gal4/VP16 alleles to their F1 progeny (Figure 4, Table 1, Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by germline transmission data.

claim: Overall germline transmission data reveal high rates of germline transmission, with a combined average of 49%, that ranged from 22–100% across all targeted loci.
source: Overall the data reveal high rates of germline transmission, with a combined average of 49%, that ranged from 22–100% across all targeted loci (Figure 4, Table 1, Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by aggregated germline transmission data across multiple loci.

claim: The founders from these experiments transmitted gametes that produced expression of RFP consistent with the targeted locus at frequencies from 2% to 64% of the F1 embryos, with an average of 17.4%.
source: In addition, the founders from these experiments transmitted gametes that produced expression of RFP consistent with the targeted locus at frequencies from 2% to 64% of the F1 embryos, with an average of 17.4% (Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data on F1 expression frequencies.

claim: Southern blot analysis and sequencing of four tyr-2A-Gal4/VP16 F1 progeny from founder F0#1 demonstrated a single copy integration of the Gal4/VP16 cassette with precise sequence at both 5' and 3' ends of the integration site.
source: Southern blot analysis and sequencing of four tyr-2A- Gal4/VP16 F1 progeny from founder F0#1 demonstrated a single copy integration of the Gal4/VP16 cassette (Table 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1) with precise sequence at both 5' and 3' ends of the integration site (Table 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by Southern blot and sequencing data.

claim: Junction fragment analysis of F1 alleles from 5 additional targeted sites revealed precise integration events at the 5' side for nearly all genes examined (35/37 or 95% across seven genes).
source: Junction fragment analysis of F1 alleles from 5 additional targeted sites in esama, flna, msna, aqp1a1, and aqp8a1 revealed precise integration events at the 5' side for nearly all genes examined (35/37 or 95% across seven genes) (Table 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: A lower frequency of precise 3' integrations (13/28 or 46% across six genes) was observed over all loci.
source: A lower frequency of precise 3' integrations (13/28 or 46% across six genes) was observed over all loci (Table 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2–4).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: Using short homology arm vectors and in vivo UgRNA liberation can promote precise, single copy integration by HMEJ at a genomic sgRNA site at high frequency in the germline.
source: Together, these results indicate that using short homology arm vectors and in vivo UgRNA liberation can promote precise, single copy integration by HMEJ at a genomic sgRNA site at high frequency in the germline, without insertion of donor vector backbone sequences, however, precision at the 3' end is reduced likely due to a lack of selection.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the aggregated data on germline transmission and junction analysis.

claim: Injection of the exon 2–4 or exon 2–25 pGTag-2A-Gal4/VP16 donor into Tg(UAS:mRFP)tpl2 embryos resulted in embryos showing broad and ubiquitous RFP expression.
source: Injection of the exon 2–4 or exon 2–25 pGTag-2A-Gal4/VP16 donor into Tg(UAS:mRFP)tpl2 embryos resulted in embryos showing broad and ubiquitous RFP expression (Figure 5b–c).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data.

claim: The frequency of RFP positive embryos was similar after targeting rb1 exon 2–4 (44–78%) and msna exon 2–6 (50–85%) and did not seem to be affected by increasing the size of the deleted region from 394 bp to 48.4 Kb in rb1 exon 2–25 (49–70%).
source: The frequency of RFP positive embryos was similar after targeting rb1 exon 2–4 (44–78%) and msna exon 2–6 (50–85%) and did not seem to be affected by increasing the size of the deleted region from 394 bp to 48.4 Kb in rb1 exon 2–25 (49–70%) (Figure 5f).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data.

claim: Somatic junction fragment analysis detected precise integration of the 2A-Gal4/VP16 cassette in both genes at the 5' upstream exon (rb1 97%; msna 85%) and 3' downstream exon (rb1 67%; msna 45%).
source: Somatic junction fragment analysis detected precise integration of the 2A-Gal4/VP16 cassette in both genes at the 5' upstream exon (rb1 97%; msna 85%) and 3' downstream exon (rb1 67%; msna 45%) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: Only one out of 16 (6%) rb1 targeted F0 founders transmitted a rb1-e2-25-2A-Gal4/VP16 integration allele through the germline.
source: However, only one out of 16 (6%) rb1 targeted F0 founders transmitted a rb1-e2-25-2A-Gal4/VP16 integration allele through the germline (Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by germline transmission data.

claim: None of the 10 msna e2-e6 2A-Gal4/VP16 targeted F0 zebrafish transmitted a deletion tagged allele to the next generation.
source: None of the 10 msna e2-e6 2A-Gal4/VP16 targeted F0 zebrafish transmitted a deletion tagged allele to the next generation (Supplementary file 1 Table S4-S5).
evidence: The claim is supported by germline transmission data.

claim: HMEJ driven by short homology arms and liberation by the UgRNA can efficiently promote precision targeted integration at a single double strand break in somatic and germline tissue.
source: While HMEJ driven by short homology arms and liberation by the UgRNA can efficiently promote precision targeted integration at a single double strand break in somatic and germline tissue, efficient simultaneous deletion and integration to bride two target sites in the germline likely occurs at a much lower frequency.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of single-site and dual-site targeting efficiencies.

claim: GFP expression was observed in 23% of porcine fibroblast colonies using the UgRNA donor, compared to 2% of colonies using the HR donor with 760 bp homology arms.
source: GFP expression was observed in 23% of colonies using the UgRNA donor, compared to 2% of colonies using the HR donor with 760 bp homology arms (Figure 6b).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data on colony GFP expression.

claim: 5' and 3' junctions were observed in over 50% of the UgRNA donor GFP+ porcine fibroblast colonies while none of the HR donor GFP+ colonies contained both junctions.
source: 5' and 3' junctions were observed in over 50% of the UgRNA donor GFP+ colonies while none of the HR donor GFP+ colonies contained both junctions (Figure 6c).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCR junction analysis data.

claim: Sequencing of junctions from 8 UgRNA donor GFP+ porcine fibroblast colonies that were positive for both junctions showed precise integration in 7/8 colonies at the 5' junction and 8/8 colonies at the 3' junction.
source: Sequencing of junctions from 8 UgRNA donor GFP+ colonies that were positive for both junctions showed precise integration in 7/8 colonies at the 5' junction and 8/8 colonies at the 3' junction.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data of junction fragments.

claim: Over 50% of K-562 cells targeted with the HMEJ 48 bp homology arm donor were GFP positive at day 14, compared to only 6% of cells electroporated with the 806 bp homology arm HR donor.
source: Over 50% of cells targeted with the HMEJ 48 bp homology arm donor were GFP positive, compared to only 6% of cells electroporated with the 806 bp homology arm HR donor, indicating HMEJ promoted efficient integration and stable expression of the MND:GFP cassette at the AAVS1 locus (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data.

claim: GFP expression in K-562 cells was maintained over 50 days.
source: GFP expression was maintained over 50 days, and 5' precise junction fragments were observed following PCR amplification in bulk cell populations (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by longitudinal flow cytometry data.

claim: The HMEJ strategy using short homology arms outperforms traditional HR techniques for targeted integration in mammalian cell systems and is effective without antibiotic selection.
source: These results demonstrate that the HMEJ strategy using short homology arms outperforms traditional HR techniques for targeted integration in mammalian cell systems and is effective without antibiotic selection.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of HMEJ and HR targeting efficiencies in mammalian cells.

claim: The pGTag vector series has been deposited at Addgene.
source: The pGTag vector series has been deposited at Addgene, and the open source protocol and homology arm website design tool are available at The Gene Sculpt suite (genescultp.org) (Mann et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is a statement of fact about resource availability.

claim: The open source protocol and homology arm website design tool are available at The Gene Sculpt suite (genescultp.org).
source: The pGTag vector series has been deposited at Addgene, and the open source protocol and homology arm website design tool are available at The Gene Sculpt suite (genescultp.org) (Mann et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is a statement of fact about resource availability.

claim: The design elements, including simultaneous double strand breaks by Cas9 at the genomic target site and vector universal sgRNA sites, and preselection of fluorescent reporter expression, may enhance the efficient recovery of germline alleles over previous reports in zebrafish.
source: Together, these design elements, that include simultaneous double strand breaks by Cas9 at the genomic target site and vector universal sgRNA sites, and preselection of fluorescent reporter expression that requires in frame fusion and precise 5' targeted integration, may enhance the efficient recovery of germline alleles over previous reports in zebrafish (Hisano et al., 2015; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is speculative about the reasons for improved efficiency compared to prior work.

claim: Positive integration events of tagged alleles are selected by fluorescence reporter expression, reflecting the endogenous pattern of expression of the targeted gene.
source: Positive integration events of tagged alleles are selected by fluorescence reporter expression, reflecting the endogenous pattern of expression of the targeted gene.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental design and observations.

claim: It is conceivable that precise events at the 3' end could preclude precise integration at the 5' end during some editing events, and vice versa.
source: Thus, it is conceivable that precise events at the 3' end could preclude precise integration at the 5' end during some editing events, and vice versa.
evidence: The claim is speculative about the mechanism of integration.

claim: These data hint at synthesis dependent strand annealing (SDSA) as a possible DNA repair mechanism for pGTag donor integration.
source: It is tempting to speculate that these data hint at synthesis dependent strand annealing (SDSA) as a possible DNA repair mechanism for pGTag donor integration (Ceccaldi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is speculative about the DNA repair mechanism involved.

claim: The inability to recover rb1 tagged alleles may have been due to the essential requirement for this tumor suppressor gene, in either somatic tissue or germline stem cells.
source: It is possible that the inability to recover rb1 tagged alleles was due to the essential requirement for this tumor suppressor gene, in either somatic tissue or germline stem cells.
evidence: The claim is speculative about the reason for lack of germline transmission.

claim: Common repetitive elements, enhancers, or a cryptic promoter in the intronic sequence of the esama 1 kb homology arms may lead to off target integration and ectopic RFP expression.
source: Common repetitive elements, enhancers, or a cryptic promoter in the intronic sequence of the esama 1 kb homology arms may lead to off target integration and ectopic RFP expression.
evidence: The claim is speculative about the cause of off-target integration.

claim: Short homology arms simplify donor vector construction and lead to efficient precision targeted integration.
source: These results underscore the utility of short homology arms, which simplifies donor vector construction and leads to efficient precision targeted integration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of short and long homology arm results.

claim: The simplicity of the strategy for building arms into the pGTag vectors, a universal guide to liberate the targeting cassette, and the GeneSculpt Suite website together will aid in streamlining targeted integration experimental design.
source: The simplicity of our strategy for building arms into the pGTag vectors, a universal guide to liberate the targeting cassette, and the GeneSculpt Suite website together will aid in streamlining targeted integration experimental design.
evidence: The claim is a statement about the utility of the developed tools.

claim: The vector suite provides a platform that can expand the zebrafish functional genomics toolkit for efficient site-directed modifications that create gene fusions, introduce cDNA variants, recombinases, or floxed gene-breaking cassettes for conditional gene inactivation.
source: Our vector suite provides a platform that can expand the zebrafish functional genomics toolkit for efficient site-directed modifications that create gene fusions, introduce cDNA variants, recombinases, or floxed gene-breaking cassettes (Clark et al., 2011) for conditional gene inactivation.
evidence: The claim is a statement about potential applications of the developed tools.

claim: Targeted integration will allow tagged or mutant genes to be expressed at endogenous levels and avoid ectopic or over-expression that can result from random transgene integration.
source: Targeted integration will allow tagged or mutant genes to be expressed at endogenous levels and avoid ectopic or over-expression that can result from random transgene integration.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about targeted vs. random integration.

claim: These tools will broaden the use of designer nucleases for homology-based gene editing at CRISPR/Cas9 and TALEN cut sites in zebrafish and mammalian cell lines.
source: These tools will broaden the use of designer nucleases for homology-based gene editing at CRISPR/Cas9 and TALEN cut sites in zebrafish and mammalian cell lines.
evidence: The claim is a statement about the potential impact of the developed tools.

claim: The results open the door for more advanced genome edits in animal agriculture and human cell lines.
source: Our results open the door for more advanced genome edits in animal agriculture and human cell lines.
evidence: The claim is a statement about the potential applications of the findings.
